---
title: Theme Provider
description: The Theme component injects design token CSS variables, loads fonts, and applies Puzzle's global styles.
---

The `Theme` component is the entry point of the theme system. It resolves tokens into CSS custom properties, renders font stylesheet links, and provides theme context to Puzzle components.

## Import

```tsx
import { Theme } from "@puzzle/theme";
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `theme` | `"light" \| "dark" \| "system"` | `"system"` | The color scheme mode. `system` follows `prefers-color-scheme`. |
| `scope` | `"root" \| "local"` | `"root"` | Whether variables apply to `:root` or only to the component's subtree. |
| `globalStyles` | `boolean` | `true` | Applies Puzzle's global base styles. Only used with root scope. |
| `tokens` | `ThemeTokenOverrides` | — | Deep-partial overrides of the default [design tokens](/docs/theme/tokens). |
| `colorTheme` | `ColorThemes` | — | One of the built-in [color themes](/docs/theme/colors#built-in-color-themes). |
| `fonts` | `Partial<Record<FontRole, FontConfig>>` | — | Google Fonts for the `heading`, `body`, and `accent` roles. See [Typography & Fonts](/docs/theme/typography). |
| `components` | `ThemeComponents` | — | Global link and image [component overrides](/docs/theme/components). |
| `nonce` | `string` | — | CSP nonce applied to the injected `<style>` elements. |

## Root scope

With the default `scope="root"`, the resolved CSS variables are assigned to `:root` and the theme applies to the whole document. This is the standard setup for an application:

```tsx
<Theme theme="system" colorTheme="emerald-forest">
  <App />
</Theme>
```

Root scope also applies Puzzle's global styles unless you opt out:

```tsx
<Theme globalStyles={false}>
  <App />
</Theme>
```

## Local scope

With `scope="local"`, the variables are assigned to a generated scope attribute instead of `:root`, and the children are wrapped in a scope element that resolves the color scheme locally. Use this to theme a single section differently from the rest of the page—for example, a permanently dark hero or an embedded preview:

```tsx
<Theme scope="local" theme="dark">
  <HeroSection />
</Theme>
```

Local scopes do not create a layout box (`display: contents`), so wrapping content in a scoped theme does not affect layout. Local scopes never apply global styles and can be nested inside a root theme; descendants inherit the scoped variables while the rest of the document keeps the root theme.

## Theme modes

- `light` — forces the light color scheme.
- `dark` — forces the dark color scheme.
- `system` — follows the user's `prefers-color-scheme` setting and updates automatically.

The active mode controls which color scheme tokens resolve into the semantic `--puzzle-color-*` variables, and sets the CSS `color-scheme` so native controls, scrollbars, and form elements match.

## Fonts

When `fonts` are provided, `Theme` renders preconnect links for Google Fonts plus one stylesheet link per configured font, and wires the resolved font families into the typography CSS variables:

```tsx
<Theme
  fonts={{
    heading: { family: "Sora", weights: [600, 700] },
    body: { family: "Inter" },
  }}
>
  <App />
</Theme>
```

## Content Security Policy

If your application uses a CSP that restricts inline styles, pass a `nonce`. It is applied to the injected `<style>` elements:

```tsx
<Theme nonce={cspNonce}>
  <App />
</Theme>
```
